facts.fact: The foreword, signed by the Minister of Information and Communications, calls the policy 'launched'; Part 4 then recommends that the government 'approve the National Digital Development Policy 2021' and replace the National ICT Policy of 2016 with it, and Part 1 records draft-policy consultation workshops held 28 September to 1 October 2021. The document names no approving act or body.
The policy text is the document hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site (mocti.gov.sl), dated 2021 on its cover.
The policy states no end date for itself, only a vision of middle-income status by 2039, and says it 'shall be reviewed every five years'.

Part 3 sets out mandates for a proposed National Digital Development Council under the President, a proposed National Digital Development Agency (NDiDA) to coordinate implementation of the National Digital Development Strategy, a Technical Working Group and a Partners Coordinating Committee; Part 4 recommends that these be approved or legally established, so the bodies are proposed, not yet stated as constituted.

The policy lists an objective 'to allocate a proportion of the national budget to develop e-government systems' and a Partners Coordinating Committee to analyse financing gaps, but states no budget line, amount or cost for the policy or the strategy; the foreword credits the Digital Impact Alliance with financial and technical support for developing the policy.

The policy contains no action or implementation plan and no costs; Part 4 instructs the Ministry of Information and Communications to 'develop the implementation plan for the NDDP' and says action plans will support the strategy and sectoral plans.

The policy reports on no progress against itself; Part 4 instructs the Ministry to develop a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework and says an M&E system based on agreed sector indicators 'shall' be developed, with periodic sector reviews built into implementation.

Part 4 says 'a digital development strategy will be developed to provide the implementation framework for this Policy', consolidating all sectors' digital plans and their resources, benchmarks, targets and responsibilities into the National Digital Development Strategy; no strategy text, adoption or drafting stage is stated.

note: Read whole including Part 3 (institutions) and Part 4 (recommendations, implementation and review). The policy is a framework: it recommends approval, proposes the bodies, and defers plan, costs and monitoring to the not-yet-written strategy. Class national on its own description (whole-of-government and whole-of-society, economy and state); the NDDS takes national because Part 4 describes it as consolidating all sectors' plans.
